question: With scarce labeled chatbot text and the same augmentation, can one CV-tuned word+character TF-IDF logistic-regression model match or beat a soft-voting ensemble of several classifiers on intent accuracy?
method: CLINC150 in-scope queries (data_small.json); 10 labeled training queries per intent subsampled from the official train split, each plus 4 random word dropout/swap copies; evaluated on the official in-scope test split; 3 seeds (subsample + augmentation).
baseline: Soft-voting ensemble of logistic regression, calibrated linear SVM and complement naive Bayes on word (1-2gram) TF-IDF, trained on original + augmented queries (stand-in for the paper's transformer ensemble).
improved: Single logistic regression on word + character TF-IDF with C in {1,10,100} chosen by 3-fold group-aware CV on the training set, same augmented data.
notes: T5/transformers and human augmentation replaced by simple random perturbation; baseline is not the paper's method. n_train is the number of original labeled queries (augmented set is 5x larger). Official val split unused; the official test split is used once per model. Baseline uses word features only and fixed hyper-parameters, so feature set and tuning both differ from the improved model. Selected C per seed: [1, 10, 10]. Std is over 3 seeds, which change the subsample and augmentation. SVM calibration inside the ensemble uses internal CV that is not group-aware.
